name: Untangle
tagline: Separate your money after a breakup, fairly and fast
about: Untangle helps couples who are splitting up divide shared money calmly: who keeps what, closing joint accounts and subscriptions, settling the deposit and the furniture, rebuilding a solo budget, and the messages that get you paid back.
persona: You are a practical, neutral separation money guide: you keep score only where it matters, protect both people from rash moves, and know when a lawyer or mediator is worth the fee.

onboarding.title: Split the money, keep your head
onboarding.subtitle: A few facts about the situation keep the advice relevant.
bullets: A fair division of shared things
Joint accounts and bills, closed cleanly

tools.title: Divide what's shared
tools.subtitle: Furniture, deposit, pets, debt

inputs.label: Shared things & money
inputs.placeholder: sofa 900 (I paid), deposit 1500 (split), joint credit card 1200 owed, the dog…

tools.prompt: Shared items and money: {items}; approach: {style}. Sections: table (Item | Who paid / whose name | Suggested outcome | Reasoning); kv (net balancing payment and who pays whom); a callout on items that are legally different from 'stuff' (joint debt, tenancy deposits, pets, anything in one name only) and which need advice given the profile's status and region; a quote with a short neutral message proposing the split.

tools.title: Close the joint stuff
tools.subtitle: Accounts, bills, subscriptions

inputs.label: Everything joint
inputs.placeholder: joint current account, Netflix on my card, energy in both names, phone family plan…

tools.prompt: Joint items: {joint}. Sections: checklist in the safest order (freeze new borrowing first, then bills, then subscriptions, then close accounts), one line per item with who does it; table (Item | Risk if left open | Action | Deadline); a callout on protecting your credit file from a joint account or shared address and on never emptying a joint account unilaterally; steps for the day you close the main joint account.

tools.title: Who stays, who goes
tools.subtitle: Rent, deposit and moving costs
tools.prompt: Home cost {rent}, deposit {deposit}, likely outcome {plan}, home situation from the profile. Sections: table (Option | Monthly cost to you | Deposit handling | Notice / moving cost | Watch-outs) comparing you staying, them staying and both leaving; kv (cash you need to leave, or to stay alone, including first month and deposit); a callout on tenancy or ownership rules that vary by region (notice, release from a joint tenancy, landlord consent, who is liable) and that this is not legal advice; a quote with a message to the landlord or agent asking what is possible.

tools.title: My solo budget
tools.subtitle: Life on one income again
tools.prompt: Rebuild a single budget: income {income}, costs {costs}. Sections: table (Category | Amount | Share of income | Adjust?); kv (left over per month, emergency-fund target for a solo household, weeks to reach it); bullets of 5 costs that quietly doubled after the split and how to soften each; a callout on the first 3 months being the expensive ones and what to tell yourself about it.

tools.title: Write the money message
tools.subtitle: Ask for what you're owed, calmly

inputs.label: What you need to say
inputs.placeholder: they owe me 400 for the last month's bills and haven't replied in 2 weeks

tools.prompt: Draft a message about: {situation}, tone {tone}. Sections: quote with the message (under 120 words, one clear ask, a date, no raking over history); bullets on what to do if there is no reply (keep a written record, mediation or small-claims as general options, when to let it go); a callout on keeping evidence (screenshots, bank records) and avoiding anything that reads as a threat.

disclaimer: General information, not legal or financial advice; separation and tenancy rules differ by country and by whether you are married — speak to a solicitor, mediator or free advice service before signing or paying anything.
